overview: Bremworth (formerly Cavalier Corporation) is a New Zealand-based premium wool and synthetic carpet manufacturer, operating alongside Elco Direct, a wool-sourcing/trading business that buys raw wool at the farm gate across the North Island. The company manufactures carpet and yarn in Whanganui, Napier and Auckland, and sells primarily to flooring retailers in New Zealand and Australia, with smaller and growing exposure to North America and China. Bremworth has spent the past three-plus years recovering from Cyclone Gabrielle plant damage while restructuring its product strategy, cost base and go-to-market approach, and is currently the subject of competing takeover proposals.

business_model.summary: Bremworth earns most of its revenue from manufacturing and selling wool and synthetic (solution-dyed nylon) broadloom carpet and rugs to flooring retailers, supplemented by Elco Direct, a wool-buying/trading operation that purchases raw wool from North Island farmers and on-sells it (including increasingly to third-party exporters). Carpet revenue is largely transactional/project-based (renovation and new-build driven, no recurring contracts), while Elco Direct revenue is volume- and wool-price-driven and has become the primary growth engine, up sharply in FY26 on a 'seismic shift' in export wool demand. Margins are thin and highly sensitive to manufacturing volume leverage, product/channel mix and wool costs.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - flooring retailers/distributors (carpet) and wool exporters/processors (Elco Direct); ultimate carpet demand is B2C residential construction and renovation
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand and Australia are the core carpet markets; Elco Direct wool sold domestically and increasingly for export; early-stage expansion into North America and China

main_competitors: Synthetic/imported carpet and hard-flooring substitutes (vinyl, laminate, LVT)
Other wool merchants/exporters competing with Elco Direct
competitive_position.market_position: Long-established premium NZ carpet brand (60+ years) but now a clear #2 to Godfrey Hirst, which management estimates makes roughly twice as much wool carpet; Godfrey Hirst's near-monopoly position in NZ wool carpet was the key antitrust concern that ultimately helped scuttle the Floorscape/Mohawk acquisition of Bremworth.

moat_factors.description: 60+ year New Zealand-made premium wool carpet brand with retailer and consumer recognition, though brand strategy has whipsawed (wool-only pivot then reversal back to wool+synthetic)
Elco Direct gives direct farm-gate wool procurement relationships built over 50+ years, providing input cost/supply advantages and an independent, now fast-growing revenue stream

Sub-scale relative to Godfrey Hirst/Mohawk; plant damage (Cyclone Gabrielle, Whanganui fire) caused years of under-recovery of fixed overheads and quality issues, only now being resolved with the Napier yarn plant back online

weaknesses: Persistently negative EBIT/EBITDA on an underlying basis for several years, with thin (13-15%) gross margins
Sub-scale vs. Mohawk-owned Godfrey Hirst in wool carpet manufacturing
History of strategic flip-flops (all-wool pivot then reversal to wool+synthetic) that confused retailers and consumers
Heavy reliance on cyclical, discretionary residential construction/renovation demand which has been subdued for several years
Governance instability: multiple board resignations and an unresolved contest for control (Mangawhai Collective vs. prior Floorscape/Mohawk scheme) creating strategic uncertainty

growth_drivers: Elco Direct wool-trading volume and export wool price momentum (the single biggest driver of FY26 revenue growth)
Re-launch of solution-dyed nylon (SDN) synthetic carpet range, with sales growth expected from FY27
Napier yarn plant now fully operational after years of Cyclone Gabrielle-related disruption, lowering product and supply chain costs and improving quality
Cost-out programme reducing the fixed cost base, expected to flow through progressively in FY27
Expanded NZ/Australia sales teams to rebuild retailer relationships and market coverage
Early-stage international expansion into North America and China
Eventual cyclical recovery in NZ/Australia residential construction and renovation activity

business.description: Carpet sales are tied to discretionary renovation and new-build activity, which has been weak across NZ and Australia for several years with no clear recovery timeline
Godfrey Hirst (Mohawk-owned) makes roughly double Bremworth's wool carpet volumes and has deep parent-company resources
Multiple strategic resets (wool-only reversal, cost programmes, sales team rebuilds) have repeatedly under-delivered against management's own targets, most recently the H1 FY26 guidance miss
Cyclone Gabrielle (2023) and a separate Whanganui yarn plant fire caused multi-year production and inventory disruption; key plants remain concentrated in Whanganui/Napier

financial.description: Normalised EBIT losses of $(9.4)m in FY26 and $(15.9)m in FY25 (underlying, ex-insurance proceeds); operating cash outflow of $(9.3)m in FY26 even after a $14.5m YoY improvement

Available cash of $22.0m at 30 June 2026 (down from $42.2m a year earlier, which included one-off insurance proceeds) provides a buffer but is being consumed by ongoing losses and capex; nil borrowings currently limits leverage risk but also reflects a small, thinly-capitalised balance sheet
Elco Direct earnings and carpet input costs are exposed to swings in raw wool prices and export demand

regulatory.description: The NZCC's scrutiny (eventually clearing, but only after a Statement of Issues and extended timeline) of the Floorscape/Mohawk acquisition on grounds it would create a near-monopoly in NZ wool carpet illustrates ongoing antitrust sensitivity around consolidation in this market

The current Mangawhai Collective partial offer (44% of shares, 90c/share) is subject to Takeovers Code conditions and is not guaranteed to complete or to be pro-rata satisfying for all accepting shareholders

macro.description: Company explicitly cites continued weakness in residential construction/renovation activity and pressured discretionary consumer spending as the main demand headwind
Higher-for-longer interest rates suppress housing turnover and renovation spending, a direct demand driver for carpet
Elco Direct's export-linked wool sales and any North America/China expansion introduce FX and international trade exposure

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ/Australia flooring and carpet demand remains subdued, tied closely to residential construction consents and renovation spending, both of which have been weak through the current rate cycle; wool carpet specifically also competes against cheaper synthetic and hard-flooring alternatives
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - carpet is a big-ticket discretionary home improvement purchase highly correlated with housing turnover, new-build activity and consumer confidence
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-high indirect sensitivity via housing/construction activity; direct balance-sheet sensitivity currently low given nil borrowings
key_input_costs: Synthetic fibre inputs (SDN yarn) for the relaunched synthetic range

recent_developments.event: Mangawhai Collective (David Ferrier, ~19.7% existing holding plus lock-up deeds over a further ~32%, ~55% total) launched a formal Rule 9 partial takeover offer for 43.94% of shares not already held, at 90c/share; Bremworth's board subcommittee recommended shareholders accept, and independent adviser Clarien Partners valued shares at 87c-$1.07, with the 90c offer inside that range. Offer open until 2 October 2026, but payment is conditional on the offer becoming unconditional.

FY26 unaudited results: revenue $106.6m (+21% YoY, Elco Direct-driven), gross margin 13.7%, net loss $(11.4)m, normalised EBIT improved to $(9.4)m from $(15.9)m, available cash $22.0m and nil borrowings
Bremworth received initial notice from Mangawhai Collective of intention to make the 90c partial takeover offer

Floorscape/Mohawk made a revised, simplified whole-company offer at 95c/share after NZCC clearance, but withdrew after a ~38% shareholder bloc (including David Ferrier and the Timpson, Harrison and Woolf families) confirmed they would vote it down; Ferrier called it 'dead on arrival' given Mangawhai's ~20% stake plus lock-ups over a further ~32%

NZ Commerce Commission ultimately cleared the original Floorscape/Mohawk scheme (after a Statement of Issues and extended decision timeline to 29 May 2026), but the scheme lapsed anyway when shareholder support collapsed and the SIA end date (extended to 7 August 2026) passed without extension

H1 FY26 results: revenue $44.7m (+6% YoY) but gross margin fell to 14.9% from 21% in pcp on adverse mix and Napier plant delays; net loss $(6.4)m; board disclosed a guidance downgrade, no longer expecting H2 FY26 to be cash-flow positive or profitable
NZCC published a Statement of Issues on the original Floorscape/Mohawk scheme, flagging competition concerns (near-monopoly risk in NZ wool carpet) and extending the review timeline

Bremworth entered into a Scheme Implementation Agreement with Floorscape Limited (backed by Mohawk Industries as guarantor) to acquire 100% of Bremworth via Scheme of Arrangement, later revised down in indicative value due to weaker trading (implied total consideration guided down from ~$0.75+$0.30-0.40 capital return to ~$0.95-1.05 total) before ultimately lapsing in mid-2026

items.notes: Board expects financial performance to improve in FY27 as benefits from revenue initiatives (SDN carpet, sales team expansion, North America/China), cost reductions and manufacturing improvements (Napier plant) progressively flow through; no specific numeric revenue/EBIT/margin target disclosed

items.target: Return to profitability and positive operating cash flow
items.notes: Stated as 'the immediate objective' alongside continued disciplined cash management; company had previously guided to a faster H2 FY26 turnaround (profitability/cash-flow positive) which it explicitly walked back in the February 2026 half-year report
Re-launched premium synthetic (solution-dyed nylon) range expected to contribute growing sales from FY27; wool remained 95% of FY26 carpet sales volumes
Management cites 'early wins' and expects these markets to deliver meaningful benefit to the company in the medium term, no quantified target

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Rob Hewett: financial result remains below Board expectations but progress has been made on operational/commercial issues; focus now on converting improvements into better margins, stronger cash generation and sustainable profitability; investment decisions assessed against clear return criteria with cash generation a central measure of management performance. CEO Craig Woolford: foundations 'considerably stronger'; focus has shifted 'from rebuilding to growth'; timing/pace of broader market recovery remains uncertain. Company has withdrawn from providing precise quantitative guidance since missing its H1 FY26 targets, and near-term outlook is further clouded by the unresolved Mangawhai Collective partial takeover.

bull_case: Elco Direct is now the primary growth engine, up sharply on strong export wool demand, and largely decoupled from the weak domestic carpet retail cycle

Multi-year operational turnaround (Napier plant restoration, cost-out programme, inventory clean-up) appears to be nearing completion, with normalised EBIT losses more than halved from FY25 to FY26 and a clear line of sight to further FY27 benefit

Independent adviser's 87c-$1.07/share valuation, and two competing takeover approaches (Floorscape at up to 95c whole-company, Mangawhai at 90c partial) within the past year, suggest sum-of-parts/private-market value may exceed the standalone public trading price, offering an M&A-driven valuation floor
Clean balance sheet with $22.0m available cash and nil borrowings gives runway to complete the turnaround without an imminent equity raise or refinancing risk
Re-launched synthetic (SDN) range and North America/China expansion open new addressable markets beyond the mature, currently depressed NZ/Australia wool carpet category
bear_case: Company has been loss-making on an underlying basis for multiple consecutive years (normalised EBITDA -$13.2m FY25, -$9.4m normalised EBIT FY26) with repeated guidance misses, most recently the H1 FY26 walk-back of a promised H2 turnaround

Structurally sub-scale versus Mohawk-owned Godfrey Hirst in its core wool carpet category, with limited pricing power and persistent gross margin pressure (13-15% range) from under-recovered fixed manufacturing costs
Demand backdrop (NZ/Australia residential construction and renovation) has been weak for years with no confirmed recovery catalyst or timeline

Ownership/control overhang: Mangawhai Collective's partial 90c offer (with ~55% effective support via stake plus lock-ups) leaves minority shareholders exposed to a controlling shareholder scenario without full exit liquidity, while the more lucrative whole-company Floorscape/Mohawk deal has already collapsed once amid shareholder infighting and board resignations

Continued cash consumption (operating cash outflow of $(9.3)m in FY26 even after improvement) against a $22.0m cash buffer means further deterioration or delayed recovery could force dilutive capital raising or renewed strategic-review pressure
